facts.text: Governor Wentworth of New Hampshire granted over twenty-three thousand acres of land to Captain Hall and sixty-three associates in November 1761.
The Wallingford House once served as a grand hotel and remains a landmark in the center of town.
Main Street and the Otter Creek Valley farming area were added to the National Register of Historic Places in the early 1980s.
The East Wallingford Railroad building houses a gasoline-powered speeder car, which replaced the hand-pump cars used by railroad maintenance workers.
Wallingford is located in Rutland County, Vermont, and contains the villages of East Wallingford and South Wallingford.
The Gilbert Hart Library and the unique Town Hall provide in-depth history regarding the buildings and community of Wallingford.
